isolation_policy: bubblewrap mount namespace: only the workspace, the policy-accepted read allowlist and the opencode runtime exist; the repository, the other arms' results, the earlier sessions and the global opencode configuration (its MCP servers and plugins) are not mounted; plus the opencode v2 permission object (bash denied, edit and write denied, read and external_directory deny-by-default with the explicit allowlist)
limitations: The mount namespace is the filesystem guarantee; the model provider is reachable over the shared network, so a model that was shown a file can still send it away.
sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT:
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: CURVCTRL-SID
TITLE: Feedback curvature: the measured hard prefix-transition score of each RQ level sets that level's negative curvature, which then reshapes the same level's quantizer metric.
MOTIVATION: A generative recommender emits a level-1 code first, then conditions on it. If the level-1 code barely predicts which level-2 code the next item carries, the generator's prefix becomes a coin flip and downstream recall collapses no matter how good the reconstruction is. Issue #126 showed that the hard prefix-transition score Q_H, computed from training-only transitions, ranks downstream test recall across seven SIDs (Spearman +0.821, exploratory). That score is currently only a DIAGNOSTIC: a proxy was built to rank prefixes, but nothing closed the loop. CURVCTRL-SID turns the hard score into the state variable of the geometry, so the quantizer's own metric is reshaped by exactly the quantity that predicts recall, at the level where the prediction fails.
NOVELTY: All earlier mechanisms put user behaviour into a per-item quantity: successor mass, transition mass, Fréchet weights, Sinkhorn cost rows, cone/tangent directions, or a prefix-rank proxy loss term. CURVCTRL-SID adds NO loss term and NO per-item behaviour weight. It uses a single per-level SCALAR measured statistic, the hard prefix hit rate Q_l of the training transition set, as the curvature of the Poincaré metric used by that same RQ level. Curvature is therefore neither a hyperparameter nor a learned parameter: it is a closed-loop controller output, recomputed each epoch from the current SID assignment. It is also the only proposal in which the geometry VARIES ACROSS RQ LEVELS, and it is the direct answer to issue #126's open question: instead of optimising the ranking proxy, the hard score is fed back as the metric in which the next assignment is made.
CHANGE: At the start of every K-th epoch we measure, per RQ level l, the fraction Q_l of training directed transitions whose two endpoints share the same level-l SID prefix, plus the mean encoder latent norm rho_l. From these two measured numbers we DERIVE a positive curvature magnitude c_l, and the level-l assignment and commitment term then use the Poincaré distance of curvature -c_l (encoder output and code vectors pushed into that ball by the origin exponential map). Poorer prefix predictability at a level means a larger c_l, which stretches the ball near its boundary and forces that level's codes to separate radially instead of only angularly.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Notation: L RQ levels (L=3 in the frozen baseline), K codes per level (K=256), N=24556 training items, d latent dim.\n1. Behaviour statistics, recomputed from the TRAINING split only, on epochs t where t mod K_meas == 0 (K_meas=5):\n   E = observed directed transitions (i -> j, i != j, consecutive within a training session), subsampled once and frozen to at most 2^20 edges by a fixed hash of (i,j) so the same sample is reused for all epochs.\n   p_l(i) = (c_1(i),...,c_l(i)) = current hard SID prefix of item i.\n   Q_l = (1/|E|) * sum over (i,j) in E of 1[ p_l(i) == p_l(j) ], clipped to [Q_min, 1], Q_min = 1e-3.\n   rho_l = (1/N) * sum over training items i of || z_l(i) ||_2, where z_l is the level-l residual input (stop-gradient).\n2. Derived curvature, one positive scalar per level:\n   c_l_raw = ( 1/Q_l - 1 ) / ( rho_l^2 + 1e-8 )\n   c_l_raw = min( c_l_raw, 0.99 / ( max_i ||z_l(i)||^2 + 1e-8 ) )   [derived cap: keeps mapped points inside the ball]\n   c_l_raw = max( c_l_raw, 1e-4 )                                    [documented floor for artanh stability]\n3. Anti-oscillation smoothing (the only other constant, a documented harmonic average, not tuned):\n   c_l <- c_l_prev + (c_l_raw - c_l_prev) / min(t + 1, 10), and c_l is additionally clipped to [c_l_prev/2, 2*c_l_prev] per update.\n4. Curved operators used at level l (curvature kappa_l = -c_l):\n   exp_0^c(z) = ( tanh( sqrt(c) * ||z|| ) / ( sqrt(c) * ||z|| + 1e-12 ) ) * z\n   x (+) y   = ( (1 + 2c<x,y> + c||y||^2) x + (1 - c||x||^2) y ) / ( 1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2 ||x||^2 ||y||^2 )\n   d_c(u,v)  = ( 2 / sqrt(c) ) * artanh( sqrt(c) * || (-u) (+) v || ), artanh argument clipped to 1 - 1e-7\n5. Quantizer at level l (this replaces only the distance; the codebook update stays the baseline Euclidean/RQ update, deliberately NOT a curved Fréchet update):\n   u = exp_0^{c_l}(z_l);  e_k = exp_0^{c_l}(e_{l,k})\n   c_l* = argmin_k d_{c_l}(u, e_k)\n   z_{l+1} = z_l - e_{l,c_l*}                        (residual stays Euclidean, standard RQ)\n   L_commit += beta * d_{c_l}(u, e_{l,c_l*})^2,  beta = 0.25 (baseline value)\n   Total loss = L_recon + L_commit + L_codebook, everything else unchanged.\n6. Switches (must exist in code; only BOTH_ON is trained):\n   behaviour_on: Q_l as measured.  behaviour_off: Q_l pinned so that c_l = 1.0 for all l (fixed unit negative curvature, no adaptation).\n   geometry_on: d_c / exp_0^c with c_l.  geometry_off: c_l := 0, exp = identity, d = squared Euclidean.'}
COST: No new parameters and no extra forward pass over the encoder. Extra per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, K=256, L=3): the level-l assignment now costs N*K = 6.29e6 curved distance evaluations instead of a dot product, i.e. 1.89e7 pairs per forward and roughly 5.7e7 with the backward, about 6-8 flops-equivalents each (two inner products, three norms, one artanh, one division) versus one inner product before. On the same GPU family this is +8 to +20 ms per step on top of a transformer step that is already tens to hundreds of ms; over 24 steps x 3000 epochs = 72000 steps that is +10 to +24 minutes of wall clock per card (the four data-parallel cards each pay it, so the run length grows by that amount, roughly 1-3 percent of Stage 2). The statistic pass is one reduction over at most 2^20 frozen edges every 5 epochs = 600 passes at about 5 ms each, under 5 s total. Memory grows only by caching one (N x d) latent per level for the norm statistics.
HYPOTHESIS: If the level-l prefix is the thing the generator has to predict, then making the level-l metric more negatively curved exactly when the measured prefix hit rate is low should force level-l codes to separate along the radial (hierarchical) direction rather than only by angle, so that a child prefix becomes more nearly a function of its parent prefix. This must show up as (a) Q_l rising over Stage 2 epochs while the behaviour-off arm's Q_l stays flat, (b) deeper levels receiving larger c_l because Q_l is non-increasing in l, and (c) Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 with no validation-based early stopping. The mechanism is worth keeping if the observed Q_l trend is monotone and the final recall clears the target; the Q_l trace, not recall alone, is what shows the loop actually ran.
RISKS: ['The main failure is that Q_l is dominated by the level-1 partition and is nearly constant across epochs, so the controller produces a near-fixed curvature and the mechanism degenerates to a fixed-curvature Poincaré quantizer; the epoch-wise Q_l trace reveals this immediately. Second, a feedback loop can oscillate or collapse onto the boundary cap, mitigated by the factor-2 clamp and harmonic smoothing but not eliminated. Third, Poincaré distances saturate near the boundary, so the commitment gradient can vanish exactly where curvature is largest; the c_l cap and float64 statistics reduce but do not remove this. Fourth, the extra distances could slow Stage 2 enough to interact with the fixed epoch budget, though the estimated overhead is small. Fifth, with one run the effect is confounded with seed noise; the Q_l trajectory is the only internal evidence that the coupling did anything.']
END IDEA

IDEA: behcone-prefix-rq
TITLE: Behaviour-entropy Poincare entailment cones as a differentiable surrogate for the first-level prefix score
MOTIVATION: Issue #126 showed that the hard hyperbolic prefix score Q_H ranks with downstream test_R@10 but left open whether a differentiable version can be optimised and whether that optimisation reaches recall. The first RQ-VAE token is the coarse cluster the generator must commit to first; if the level-1 codebook is organised so that a prefix's observed successors fall inside its own curved "future cone", the first token becomes behaviourally predictive instead of only reconstruction-optimal.
NOVELTY: The earlier rounds used successor mass inside Sinkhorn, successor-weighted Fréchet codebook updates, curved residuals, geodesic charts, Lorentz cones and branch curvature. This proposal is not a cone quantizer and not a mass-weighted assignment: it keeps the RQ-VAE quantizer unchanged and adds a behaviour-conditioned aperture to a Poincare entailment cone on the level-1 codewords, so that the aperture itself is a measured function of the training-only prefix-transition entropy (no swept constant), and the cone penalty is the differentiable proxy for the hard Q_H of Issue #126. Prefix-to-prefix pairs (not item pairs) make the whole penalty act on the codebook only.
CHANGE: Build a directed level-1 prefix transition matrix from training-split item transitions, turn each row into a successor distribution, and add to the RQ-VAE objective a hyperbolic entailment-cone penalty that pushes each observed successor prefix into the cone rooted at the source prefix, with half-aperture alpha_k = arctan(exp(H_k/log(K+1) - 1)) taken from that row's entropy.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "See SPEC EQUATIONS. Inputs: level-1 codebook C in R^{K x d} (K codewords, d dim), training-split transition counts N_ij, a curvature c=1 Poincare ball. Precompute once: M_kk' = sum_{i in k, j in k'} N_ij with k = prefix1(i), k' = prefix1(j) from the current codeword assignment, so M is refreshed every 100 epochs (cheap, 24.6k items). Per step: sample up to 256 source prefixes with >=20 transitions, take their top-8 successors by M mass, evaluate the cone penalty, backprop into C. No encoder or decoder change."}
COST: One extra pass every 100 epochs over 24556 items to refresh M (O(#transitions), seconds). Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, batch ~1023, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs): at most 256 source prefixes x 8 successors = 2048 Poincare log/angle evaluations of dimension d plus one scalar entropy per source row; this is under 1% of the RQ-VAE forward+backward flops and adds roughly 2-4% wall clock. 72000 steps total; no extra model, no extra encoder forward pass for successor items.
HYPOTHESIS: If the hard Q_H-to-recall relation is causal and not a small-sample artefact, then a differentiable cone proxy that is optimised during Stage 2 should (i) raise cone containment and lower the level-1 successor rank of held-out training transitions, (ii) raise the Issue #126 hard Q_H evaluated on the resulting SID, and (iii) lift Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 with the same single run. If Q_H only correlates because both are driven by item popularity, Q_H will move but recall will not.
RISKS: ['The cone penalty may collapse many prefixes toward the boundary or make level-1 codes redundant, hurting reconstruction and prefix counts; behaviour sparsity (first-level prefixes with few transitions) can make entropy and aperture noisy; the aperture could be gamed by pushing entropy down instead of structuring the geometry (mitigated by stopping the gradient through alpha); the effect may be too weak at level 1 alone.']
END IDEA

IDEA: succboost-geoshift
TITLE: Behavioural-diffuseness geodesic pre-shift of item latents before a Poincare residual quantiser, so level-1 prefixes fill with behaviourally predictable items.
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE level-1 prefixes are the token the generative recommender emits first, and a level-1 cell that mixes a niche item with a hub is untrainable: the cell's successor distribution is smeared by the hub, so the first token carries little information. Issue #126 established that the hard hyperbolic first-level prefix score Q_H ranks with downstream test_R@10 (Spearman +0.821 on seven SIDs), which says the geometric separation of the level-1 partition is the quantity worth changing - yet all seven SIDs shared one radial layout. Here the radial layout itself is set by a training-only behaviour statistic, so level-1 capacity is spent on items whose continuation is predictable and fine-level capacity on items whose continuation is diffuse.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds moved behaviour into the assignment mass (successor-diffused Poincare Sinkhorn), into the codebook update (successor-weighted curved Fréchet means), into per-branch and per-level curvature, into tangent/gyro targets, into Lorentz cones, into the prefix score itself, into geodesic charts and into code repair. None changed WHERE an item sits along the ball's radial geodesic as a function of behaviour. This is a per-item curved displacement (an explicit exp map along the item's own radial geodesic) applied to the latent before any assignment exists; the hyperbolic quantiser is only the substrate, and the new object is a deterministic behaviour-conditioned geodesic displacement field - not a loss term, not a codebook rule, not an assignment weight.
CHANGE: Each item gets a frozen scalar beta_i = gamma*(cbar - c_i) from the concentration of its training successor distribution; every training step moves the latent along its own radial geodesic by hyperbolic distance beta_i, z'_i = exp_{z_i}(beta_i * rhat_i), and only z'_i is quantised by the Poincare residual chain. Capacity redistributes across levels: concentrated items stay near the origin where level-1 codes live, diffuse items are pushed into the exponentially large outer region and must be resolved by levels 2-3.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Fixed curvature K = -1/R^2 with R = 0.9 (documented default, never tuned). Encoder head z = R*u/(1+||u||) so ||z|| < R with no tanh saturation. Offline once, before epoch 1: directed transition counts T[i,j] from consecutive items inside training sessions only; Laplace-smoothed successor distribution p_i(j) = (T[i,j]+1)/(sum_j T[i,j] + |Succ(i)|); concentration c_i = 1 - H(p_i)/log|Succ(i)| in [0,1]; cbar, sigma = mean and std of c_i over items with at least one successor; gamma = clip(1/sigma, 0.5, 8); beta_i = clip(gamma*(cbar - c_i), -1, 1); items with no successor row get beta_i = 0. Per step: rhat_i = z_i/max(||z_i||,1e-8); z'_i = z_i (+) (R*tanh(beta_i/(2R)) * rhat_i) with Möbius addition at curvature -1/R^2; clamp ||z'_i|| into [1e-3 R, 0.999 R]; then the usual three-level chain r_1 = z'_i, k_l = argmin_k d_P(r_l, c_{l,k}), r_{l+1} = r_l (+) (-c_{l,k_l}), zhat = c_1k1 (+) c_2k2 (+) c_3k3, SID(i) = (k1,k2,k3). Loss, optimiser, learning rate, ordering, epoch count and the Stage-3 protocol are unchanged; only the quantiser's input changes. Switches: BEHAVIOUR=off sets beta_i = 0; GEOMETRY=off replaces the exp map by Euclidean dilation z_i*exp(beta_i) and d_P by squared Euclidean. Both switches exist and are unit-tested; no arm is trained with them off this round."}
COST: One frozen run, one seed, no sweep. Per step the batch is 24556/24 ≈ 1023 items: 1023 exp maps (elementwise, O(d)) plus 3 × 1023 × 256 ≈ 7.9e5 Poincare distances instead of squared Euclidean ones, so the only added transcendental is arcosh on a kernel that is a small fraction of encoder/decoder cost: roughly +4 to +6 percent step time and under 5 percent of wall clock over 3000 epochs × 24 steps = 72k steps, plus a one-off beta precompute of a few seconds over the training transition pairs. Memory adds one frozen float and one unit vector per item plus one latent buffer.
HYPOTHESIS: It is worth keeping only if the encoder does not cancel the shift and the shift buys prefix sharpness. Concretely, the post-training rank correlation between beta_i and hyperbolic radius artanh(||z_i||/R) must stay clearly positive (target > 0.3; near zero means the encoder inverted the displacement and the mechanism is inert), and level-1 successor purity (share of training transitions whose endpoints share the level-1 code) must rise together with Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. If radius tracks behaviour but recall is flat, the reallocation is real but the generator cannot exploit it.
RISKS: ['The encoder controls z and can compensate the shift by pulling high-beta items inward, cancelling the effect (that is exactly why the radius-beta correlation is recorded). Pushing diffuse items outward can crowd the outer shell, inflate level-2/3 collisions and starve the mid radius, giving dead level-1 codes and a level-1 usage-entropy collapse. arcosh is numerically hostile near the boundary. Laplace-smoothed concentration is noisy for low-degree items, and sigma dominated by the many one-successor items makes gamma small and the shift weak. Finally a better prefix partition need not survive the frozen Stage-3 generator, which may simply re-learn the SID marginal.']
END IDEA

IDEA: LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ
TITLE: SIDs quantised from the Lorentzian centre of mass of an item's successor-profile twins
MOTIVATION: Two items can be behaviourally interchangeable — their next-item distributions match — while sitting far apart in content space, so a Euclidean RQ-VAE hands them unrelated level-1 prefixes and the Stage-3 generator cannot use "this is an X-intent item" as a cheap first token. Issue #126 measured that the hard hyperbolic first-level prefix score Q_H ranks with downstream test_R@10 (Spearman +0.821, small sample), which says the level-1 partition, not the deeper digits, is where recall is decided. The unaddressed gap: the point that actually enters the quantiser is a single item's content vector, never a behaviour-consensus position, so behaviourally equivalent items cannot be pulled into one cell at the level that matters.
NOVELTY: The earlier rounds occupied (i) soft/OT assignment mass, (ii) codebook centroid updates (Fréchet/Karcher), (iii) curvature as a function of branching, (iv) residual transport and geodesic charts, (v) a post-hoc prefix-rank proxy. None of them changed *which point is quantised*. Here the behaviour signal is moved upstream into the geometry of the quantiser input: the item's hyperboloid point is replaced by its Lorentzian weighted midpoint over a successor-PROFILE-equivalence neighbourhood, and the same curvature that forms that midpoint also defines the assignment metric and the residual chain. It also differs from a GNN feature-smoothing trick: the smoothing is not preprocessing of features, it is the exp/log/pseudosphere arithmetic that generates the residual chain, and the codebooks live on the same hyperboloid. The behaviour relation is successor-profile similarity (Hellinger/cosine of row-normalised transition rows), not raw directed edges — raw edges, which every earlier round used, conflate "co-occurs with" with "behaves alike".
CHANGE: Lift the encoder output to the hyperboloid, replace it by a 50/50 Minkowski convex combination with its K successor-profile twins, re-project onto the hyperboloid, and run the entire residual-quantisation chain (Lorentzian-distance assignment, log_0 residual) on that smoothed point.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'kappa = 1 (documented default: one unit of curvature in latent units), alpha = 0.5 (documented default: equal trust between own content and behaviour twins), K = round(median positive out-degree) measured from the training transition matrix, twins from cosine similarity of sqrt of row-normalised training transition profiles, whole graph frozen before Stage 2; full equations in SPEC EQUATIONS.'}
COST: Frozen scale, B = ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items per step, L levels, C codes per level, latent d = 32, K neighbours. Smoothing gather/combine B*K*(d+1) ≈ 1023*8*33 ≈ 2.7e5 MAC per step ≈ 1% of the existing B*L*C*d ≈ 1023*3*256*32 ≈ 2.5e7 MAC assignment. The Lorentzian assignment replaces the Euclidean one at the same order (B*L*C*(d+1) vs B*L*C*d), so step overhead is under 2% of the quantiser and under 1% of a full Stage-2 step; the epoch-start table refresh is one no-gradient encoder pass (24 batches) = +4.2% encoder forward per epoch. One-off graph build (sparse P·Pᵀ on a 24556×24556 transition matrix, ~5e5 nnz) is 1–3 min CPU, a few hundred MB, once. Over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72k steps this is baseline + ~5% wall clock, no memory growth.
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviourally interchangeable items should share the level-1 token, then smoothing the quantiser input along successor-profile edges will (a) raise the share of successor-linked pairs that share a level-1 code, (b) raise the issue-#126 Q_H recomputed on the new SIDs, and (c) push the single frozen Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. Observed through the three diagnostics plus the one test run; if Q_H rises but recall does not, the level-1 partition is not the binding constraint.
RISKS: ['(a) Smoothing can wash out content identity, raising reconstruction error until the SID carries too little item-specific information and Stage 3 loses precision at rank 10; (b) the transition graph is sparse and popularity-skewed, so twin sets are noisy and hub items dominate the consensus; (c) alpha = 0.5 must be right on the first attempt because no sweep is permitted; (d) per-epoch staleness of the neighbour table lets the smoothed point lag the encoder; (e) K = median out-degree can be large, in which case the twin set is diluted.']
END IDEA
